body:
This looks great!

I did some experimentation on how to speed it up further, here's a modified `benchmark.sh` and the results on my AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS laptop: [benchmark.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26927638/benchmark.sh)


```
map, no wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 354 msec per loop
for loop, no wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 417 msec per loop
map, re wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 410 msec per loop
for loop, re wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 475 msec per loop
for loop, textwrap
1 loop, best of 5: 3.13 sec per loop
```

So basically we can shave off ~15% more by using `map(str, buffer)` instead of `str(byte) for byte in buffer`.

And the cost of wrapping seems to be around 12% with the `re` approach, which seems fine.
I'm not sure we need to bother wrapping in practice (maybe at least after 1000+ chars to avoid super long lines) but it's not too costly now so we can leave it as is.

> So basically we can shave off ~15% more by using map(str, buffer) instead of str(byte) for byte in buffer.

Awesome! I see similar results on my machine:
```
map, no wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 1.11 sec per loop
for loop, no wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 1.31 sec per loop
map, re wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 1.29 sec per loop
for loop, re wrap
1 loop, best of 5: 1.4 sec per loop
for loop, textwrap
1 loop, best of 5: 7.97 sec per loop
```
(same settings as per OP, on battery tho if that makes a difference)

That's a ~6x improvement now, compared to the previous ~5.6x. Thank you! I can see that you have an even better factor of improvement, no idea about why.

I'll update the PR shortly.

>  I'm not sure we need to bother wrapping in practice (maybe at least after 1000+ chars to avoid super long lines) but it's not too costly now so we can leave it as is.

I didn't want to risk breaking compatibility (especially with MSVC being very picky about stuff), so I kept the output as similar as close to the old behavior.

Actually, thinking about it I'm not sure if wrapping to longer lines would help with performance. I guess that the RE capture would be bigger and thus be slower. Doing more stuff in the script instead of offloading everything to the runtime might be slow too. That's the tricky thing with scripting.

Actually if it weren't for our needs of portability, we could use other methods. I did some research and there are quite a few faster ways to embed files, but they become less and less standard (and thus less portable, I assume).

In order of speed (AFAICT), we could:

 * Using `objcopy` (or similar tools) to generate an object file, linking it directly, and accessing the generated symbols through `extern`, skipping the compiler altogether. This is probably the "best" way (outside of `#embed`), although it's platform dependent.[^incbin]

 * Using the `.incbin` assembler directive. GCC (and many compilers) allow it in inline asm blocks. This seems like a suprisingly universal solution (save for MSVC). [incbin](https://github.com/graphitemaster/incbin) (under the Unlicense) seems like a nice way to use this approach and also tries to address MSVC's shortcomings.[^incbin]

 * Using a huge string literal like the output of [bin2c](https://github.com/adobe/bin2c/). explain the approach although the the tool linked there ([strliteral](https://github.com/mortie/strliteral)) doesn't have a license. Unfortunately this approach might hit weird string length limits in some compilers like MSVC.[^fast-cpp-embeds]

Given that generated headers still need to be compiled (and are apparently pretty heavy), I'm curious about the savings of the `objcopy` method.

Perhaps we could have text generation by default and allow specific platforms (or compilers?) to take over and implement their specific optimized approach. That would keep compatibility with obscure platforms (consoles?) while allowing the "main" platforms to benefit from faster compilation time.

[^fast-cpp-embeds]: https://mort.coffee/home/fast-cpp-embeds/
[^incbin]: https://www.devever.net/~hl/incbin

Edit: Found another good summary of most methods: https://andersch.dev/article/embedding-binary-files-in-c/

@akien-mga I've added a "thank you" in the commit description. Please tell me if you'd prefer a co-authored tag. (I'm going by the "should this person be held accountable for the commit" rule of thumb)
